Keyboard & Mouse Navigation

Standard motion capture and analysis shortcuts (Mokka & Visual3D compatible):

Space
Play / Pause motion playback
← / →
Step one frame backward / forward
Home / End
Jump to start / end of trial
Drag
Orbit camera view (yaw and pitch)
Shift + Drag
Pan camera across scene
Wheel
Zoom camera in / out
R
Reset camera and center on subject
G
Toggle ground plane grid
L
Toggle marker label tags
T
Toggle active marker trail
B
Toggle skeleton / stick figure bones
D
Toggle distance measurement line (Marker A–B)
C
Cycle marker color (11 colors from viewc3d)
+ / -
Increase / decrease marker size
Alt + T
Toggle Light / Dark theme mode
Alt + K
Open Segment Bases & Kinematics dialog
Alt + L
Open Reference System & Origin dialog
Alt + F
Open Signal Filtering & Gap Fill dialog
Esc
Close open dialog / modal window

Origin Translation (Meters)

Smooth, Filter & Gap Fill (interp_smooth_split)

Biomechanics signal conditioning pipeline: Hampel outlier spike removal, interpolation of missing frames, and zero-phase Butterworth smoothing.

1. Outlier Spike Removal (Hampel Filter)
2. Missing Frames Gap Filling (Interpolation)
3. Signal Smoothing Filter
6.0 Hz
Sampling rate: 100 Hz (Nyquist: 50 Hz)
0.30
Constant-velocity Kalman smoother (forward filter + RTS backward pass). No extra parameters — tuned for typical marker trajectory noise.

📐 Segment Bases (s1, s2, sg) & Kinematics

Create unlimited secondary / virtual points using NumPy formulas (e.g. (p['RASI'] + p['LASI']) / 2). These points can be selected as origins or axes to define segment bases.

Create New Point
Quick Formula Templates:
0 points defined
No virtual points defined yet.
Name Formula Status Action

Each basis is built from 3 non-collinear points and strictly orthonormalized (90° between axes, unit norm ||e|| = 1.0 via Euclidean norm division, right-handed det = +1).

Global System (sg) — Laboratory Real World
✓ Orthonormal Lab System (det = +1.0)
Local System 1 (s1) — Proximal Segment
✓ Orthonormal 90.0° (||ex||=1.000, ||ey||=1.000, ||ez||=1.000, det=+1.000)
Local System 2 (s2) — Distal Segment
✓ Orthonormal 90.0° (||ex||=1.000, ||ey||=1.000, ||ez||=1.000, det=+1.000)
Scale: 0.12 m
Mathematical Formulation:
MR2 = sg · s1T
MR = (MR2 · s2) · sgT = sg · s1T · s2 · sgT
Relative joint rotation matrix expressing Segment 2 in Segment 1 transformed to the Laboratory reference system.

Export all computed segment bases, relative rotation matrices, Euler angles, and Quaternions to CSV for external analysis, or generate a standalone reusable Python pipeline script.

Kinematics CSV Export

Full frame-by-frame data: origins (s1, s2), basis matrices (s1, s2, sg), relative rotation matrices (MR2, MR), Cardan/Euler angles, and scalar-first Quaternions.

Python Pipeline Script (.py)

Self-contained Python script replicating all virtual points, Gram-Schmidt bases, and MR calculations with NumPy. Runnable on any machine without GUI.
